findings.title: Idle workers can drop retained pipes without recording cleanup uncertainty
findings.summary: HIGH operational must-fix; confidence9/10; rubric25, with the same consequence qualifying rubric32. Retained-endpoint accounting occurs only inside PipeIo::transfer after cancellation. An escaped/reparented adapter descendant can retain stdin's read end alone, close stdout/stderr and remain alive while no write is in flight. Explicit close wakes the idle writer, which returns immediately on the non-live state and drops its PipeIo without another transfer. The captured tree terminates and all workers join, but cancellation.retained remains false. finish then makes cleanup_complete true, so reserve stops charging that instance against the eight-slot ceiling despite the still-live retainer. The current regression holds all three endpoints and blocks a64KiB write; it does not cover this idle-writer path. This is false cleanup/resource-admission accounting, not a demand to discover or kill arbitrary escaped PIDs.

evidence.label: Reachable adapter-controlled source
evidence.explanation: The adapter controls inherited child-stdio endpoints. The existing fixture demonstrates a setsid/fork/reparented process outside captured ancestry/session. The same process shape can close stdout/stderr, retain stdin only and park; after ordinary initialization the writer can be idle with an empty output queue. No payload or reproduction was executed by this reviewer.

evidence.label: Broken endpoint-lifetime control
evidence.explanation: Close marks state non-live and wakes the writer before the owner finishes tree termination. The idle writer returns without any subsequent PipeIo::transfer call. There is no final owner-side inspection or Drop classification for the endpoint before it is discarded; dropping the shared wake sender cannot classify a worker that already returned.

evidence.label: False completion reaches admission
evidence.explanation: With root/known members terminated, stdout/stderr at EOF and all handles joined, run sees no retained flag and records no cleanup failure. finish sets joined. cleanup_complete excludes only cleanup/process-identity failures, and reserve counts cleanup-complete instances as ended rather than charged. Repeated open/close operations can therefore leave retainers outside the stated charging boundary.

evidence.label: Nearby test does not close the gap
evidence.explanation: The retained-pipe regression calls s04_held_prompt before close/shutdown, leaving a writer blocked on64KiB while a retainer holds all three descriptors. Its cancellation flag is necessarily observable through active I/O. Those meaningful parent RED/GREEN results do not cover returning from an idle writer without another transfer.

findings.remediation: Retain endpoint observability until known-tree termination and final classification of every owned pipe, including idle-worker, reader early-return and partial-start exits. Record a still-held endpoint as incomplete/failed cleanup before releasing its descriptor and keep the instance charged. Preserve prompt cancellation, full worker joins and birth-qualified signalling; do not write probe payloads, detach workers or signal uncaptured PIDs. Parent should add real-child stdin-only/idle-writer regressions for close and direct shutdown, plus stdout-only/early-reader-exit coverage, asserting retainer liveness, truthful cleanup metadata and continued capacity charging before explicit fixture release. Update the general documentation/evidence claim to match the repaired coverage.
